description:
As a community, the University of Rochester is defined by a deep commitment to Meliora - Ever Better. Embedded in that ideal are the values we share: equity, leadership, integrity, openness, respect, and accountability. Together, we will set the highest standards for how we treat each other to ensure our community is welcoming to all and is a place where all can thrive.
 
 Job Location (Full Address): 
 
250 East River Rd, Rochester, New York, United States of America, 14623 
 Opening: 
 
 Worker Subtype:
Regular 
 Time Type:
Full time 
 Scheduled Weekly Hours:
40 
 Department:
250548 LLE-Laboratory for Laser Energ 
 Work Shift:
UR - Day (United States of America) 
 Range:
UR URG 116 
 Compensation Range:
$109,000.00 - $163,600.00 
 The referenced pay range represents the minimum and maximum compensation for this job. Individual annual salaries/hourly rates will be set within the job's compensation range, and will be determined by considering factors including, but not limited to, market data, education, experience, qualifications, expertise of the individual, and internal equity considerations. 







 
 
 Responsibilities: 
 
Manages a team that designs, develops, tests, debugs, and implements software that supports the operation of LLE’s world class Omega Laser Facility, research laboratories, and associated laboratory equipment. 

Determines systems software design requirements. Ensures that system improvements are successfully implemented and monitored to increase efficiency. Generates systems software engineering policies, standards, and procedures. Assures adherence to existing security, compliance, and regulatory requirements. Participates in all aspects of software development, from detailed programming to high-level system design. Oversees the performance and results of a team within own discipline or function. Adapts departmental plans and priorities to address resource and operational challenges. Provides technical guidance to employees, colleagues, and/or customers. 
 
 ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS 
 Provides day-to-day oversight of the respective Lines of Business (LOBs). Assists leadership in allocating personnel and manages and/or assigns team resources.  Contributes to a world-class research organization, assisting in continuous process improvement initiatives and refinement of service offerings. Leads the team in creating and adopting architectural patterns and software engineering best practices while holding the team accountable for those same standards.
 Manages the full software development lifecycle, including planning, design, development, testing, deployment, and maintenance. Ensures adherence to software engineering best practices, coding standards, and architectural patterns. Works with cross-functional teams, including product management, IT, and academic departments, to define technical requirements and deliver solutions. Oversees the integration of new software applications and enhancements to existing systems. Participates in project, manage risks, and ensure successful project completion.
 Works closely with product management to ensure alignment between business goals and technical execution. Partners with internal department operations and other departments to ensure seamless integration and deployment of software products. Communicates effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, ensuring clarity on goals, challenges, and progress.
 Identifies emerging technologies, industry trends, and innovative practices that can be integrated into the organization’s software development processes. Empowers teams to think beyond traditional approaches, embrace continuous improvement, and iterate quickly while maintaining high standards of quality and performance. Champions initiatives that support collaboration, knowledge sharing, and mentorship, creating an environment where engineers feel inspired. Encourages creative problem-solving and experimentation and, in turn, drives the development of cutting-edge solutions.
 Run an On-Call rotation and serves as escalation and primary communicator to IT Leadership and other executives. Assists leadership in directing the technical team and coordinates the collection of labor and expense details. Maintains shared responsibility for the uninterrupted operation of the Omega Laser Facility and LLE’s developed software systems.
 Other duties as assigned.
 
 MINIMUM EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE 
 Bachelor's degree related discipline such as Computer Science, Business, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Instructional Technology and 3 years of relevant experience required
 Master's degree preferred
 Or equivalent combination of education and experience
 Previous experience in a supervisory capacity preferred
 
 KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES 
 Expertise with technology in the respective area required
 Experience building programs that deliver long term success required
 Ability to learn new technologies quickly required
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills, as well as speaking and presentation skills required
 Ability to present technology in non-technical terms and recognize the extent to which a given audience requires this required
 Excellent customer service skills, including the ability to diffuse difficult situations required
 Ability to translate user needs into solution requirements required
 Ability to lead a team to produce valuable results required
 Ability to provide on-call support as necessary required
 Ability to handle multiple tasks at one time and meet required deadlines required
 
 The University of Rochester is committed to fostering, cultivating, and preserving an inclusive and welcoming culture to advance the University’s Mission to Learn, Discover, Heal, Create – and Make the World Ever Better. In support of our values and those of our society, the University is committed to not discriminating on the basis of age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, military/veteran status, national origin, race, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, citizenship status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law (Protected Characteristics). This commitment extends to non-discrimination in the administration of our policies, admissions, employment, access, and recruitment of candidates, for all persons consistent with our values and based on applicable law.
